author: qwen3-coder-next
voice: a developer on the team who owns the admin API, writing to a teammate
brief: Phase: long multi-phase, idea to ship. Role: developer. Repo: a Node.js billing-settings admin API where staff change account settings (tax ids, invoice contacts, payment terms, API secrets). The ask: an audit trail of every change (who, when, what changed as before and after values, request id), a query endpoint with paging, a retention period, and masking of sensitive values. Traps to plant (adapt, five or more): (1) settings change through three code paths (the REST handler, a CSV bulk import, a nightly scheduled job) and two of them skip the service layer; (2) docs/data-classes.md lists which fields are secret or personal, and the existing logger masks only fields named `password`; (3) nested settings objects need a before/after diff, not whole-object copies; (4) system jobs have no human actor and the current code puts `undefined`; (5) config has a retention number of days and a legal-hold flag per account, and the purge must skip held accounts; entries need a monotonic sequence because timestamps collide. Decisions the design note must settle: where the trail is written, what is masked and how, retention and holds, who may read it. The feature is built end to end: the request asks for a short design note, the feature with tests, a rollout plan and a release note.
